audit.why: Difficulty is correctly written as a survive-then-spike lane: Siphoning Strike (Q) drops from 7.5s to 3.5s with rank and resets his auto, so he farms and stacks through a Malphite who has no level 1-3 trade pattern. The audited mirror at audits/top/nasus__malphite.json reaches the same shape from his side, so the two pages agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart is inverted against this matchup's own prose and against the audited mirror. content.win reads Malphite, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite, Skill, Nasus, Nasus and full.phases sides match it — yet content.early opens 'Nasus owns levels 1-3' and content.mid calls Level 6 'your real spike'.
audit.why: The mirror audit for nasus vs malphite states the agreed shape explicitly: Nasus early, Malphite around 6 and first item, Nasus late. The current Malphite chart says he wins levels 1 through 5 and loses from first item, which is the opposite of every sentence on his own page and would put the two directions in direct contradiction. I did not submit the fix as edits because each cell is a one-word enum and the ±10% length band would reject 'Skill' becoming 'Malphite'; the target array is recorded here instead.
audit.corrected: win and phases sides should read: Nasus, Nasus, Nasus, Skill, Malphite, Malphite, Nasus.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Fire (E) is never mentioned in either layer.
audit.why: Spirit Fire is a flat 12s zone that reduces the armour of everyone standing on it. Ground Slam's damage scales off Malphite's own armour, so Nasus dropping Spirit Fire under Malphite is not just a durability tax, it directly shrinks Malphite's damage. That makes stepping off the zone before casting E a concrete sequencing rule, and it is the one Nasus ability the page had no opinion about.
audit.corrected: Spirit Fire (E), flat 12s, cuts your armour — and your armour is Ground Slam's damage. Step off it before you slam.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer says what Ground Slam actually does to Nasus specifically, and neither carries its cooldown.
audit.why: Ground Slam is flat 7s at every rank. Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack and Soul Eater is lifesteal on basic attacks, so a single attack-speed cut taxes his damage and his sustain simultaneously. It is the most anti-Nasus button Malphite owns and it is available roughly twice as often as anything Nasus can answer it with. The mirror audit raised the same gap from the other side.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam (E): flat 7s, and its attack-speed cut hits his Q autos and his Soul Eater lifesteal in one button.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states what Wither can and cannot do to Unstoppable Force.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is an unstoppable dash — a slow applied as it is cast does not shorten the travel or cancel the knock-up. What Wither takes away is the follow-up, which is where all of Malphite's damage lives. The mirror audit corrected the same misconception on the Nasus side, so both pages now describe one interaction with the same timing logic: the dash always arrives, the follow-up is what gets deleted.
audit.corrected: Expect Wither the instant you land. The dash cannot be slowed; the follow-up can, so R only when the kill or the gank is already there.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns listed Wither with no number and then two placeholder lines about 'your committal tool' and 'your ultimate'.
audit.why: The numbers that run this lane are Wither 15/14/13/12/11, Spirit Fire flat 12s, Ground Slam flat 7s, and Unstoppable Force 130/115/100 against Fury of the Sands 120/100/80 — his ultimate is up more often than yours at every rank, which is the opposite of the assumption 'hold R for the fight' implies.
audit.corrected: Wither 15/14/13/12/11; Spirit Fire flat 12s; your Ground Slam flat 7s; your R 130/115/100 against his 120/100/80.

audit.why: 51.58% over 1138 games. The mirror records 53.85% over 1196 games from the Nasus side of the same pairing; the two figures come from different sample rows and I did not reconcile them, but neither page's advice depends on the gap.

edits.before: Nasus owns levels 1-3 here — his empowered Q gives him a free last-hit and a stack while you have no trade button at all, so do not try to contest him at melee range. Granite Shield only refreshes when you back off, so eat the occasional auto, deny what Q stacks you can with your own last-hits, and never walk into a Wither — that slow shuts off any kiting or escape you have pre-6. This is a farm-and-survive window; your job is to reach 6 with a healthy CS, not to fight.
edits.after: Nasus owns levels 1-3 — Siphoning Strike (Q) is an auto-attack reset on 7.5s that gives him a free harder last-hit and a stack while you have no trade button, so do not contest him at melee range. Granite Shield only refreshes when you back off, so eat the occasional auto, deny what stacks you can, and never walk into Wither. Watch Spirit Fire (E) too: a flat 12s zone that cuts your armour, and Ground Slam's damage is your armour.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stabilize as W Thunderclap and E Ground Slam come online — Ground Slam's attack-speed slow directly cuts his Q-auto DPS, so you can finally farm through him and even chunk him with empowered W autos. Level 6 is your real spike: Unstoppable Force plus your Q slow turns a passive lane into an all-in or a clean gank setup, and Nasus has no dash to escape your knock-up. Force a fight or a roam here while his stacks are still low and his Wither is your only thing to dodge.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stabilize as W Thunderclap and E Ground Slam come online — Ground Slam is a flat 7s and its attack-speed slow taxes both halves of him at once, his Siphoning Strike autos and his Soul Eater lifesteal. Level 6 is your real spike: Unstoppable Force is 130s to his 120s, so spend it on a kill or a gank, not a trade. Expect Wither the instant you land — the dash cannot be slowed, but everything after it can. Do not shove into his tower with his jungler unknown.

edits.before: This is Nasus's game and you have to accept it. A stacked Nasus's Q does max-HP damage that eats straight through your armor, his Wither cripples your move and attack speed so your Ground Slam slow stops mattering, and R lifesteal lets him out-sustain anything your kit does in a straight 1v1. Stop trying to duel him — your value is now your R. Build armor, peel, and flank his carries to open fights; let your team handle the giant dog while you do what Malphite actually does well.
edits.after: This is Nasus's game and you have to accept it. Stop trying to duel him — your value is now your R. Build armour, peel, and flank his carries; let your team handle the giant dog while you start the fight.
